title: Mock 3 · Process & Products
blurb: Corpus maths, life cycle funds, NPS intermediaries, and the small-savings and grievance basics.

questions.q: The Project OASIS report, which recommended moving from unfunded defined-benefit promises to a funded defined-contribution system with individual portable accounts, was prepared by a committee chaired by:
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment set up a committee in 1998 chaired by S.A. Dave; its 2000 report is known as the Project OASIS Report.
hints: Wrong: not associated with Project OASIS in the workbook.
Wrong: not associated with Project OASIS in the workbook.
Wrong: not associated with Project OASIS in the workbook.
Correct: S.A. Dave chaired the OASIS committee.

questions.q: The FIRE movement in personal finance stands for:
questions.explanation: FIRE stands for Financial Independence, Retire Early: saving and investing aggressively (often 50% or more of income) to retire well before the conventional age.
hints: Wrong: not the expansion of FIRE.
Wrong: FIRE is voluntary, not forced early retirement.
Correct: Financial Independence, Retire Early.
Wrong: not the expansion of FIRE.

questions.q: A SEBI-registered REIT must distribute at least what share of its net distributable cash flows to unitholders?
questions.explanation: Not less than 90% of the net distributable cash flows of the REIT are distributed to investors at least on a half-yearly basis.
hints: Wrong: the requirement is not 100% quarterly.
Correct: at least 90%, at least half-yearly.
Wrong: 80% is the minimum share of completed, rent-generating assets.
Wrong: the share is far higher than 50%.

questions.q: To encourage retail participation, what share of each government securities auction is reserved for non-competitive bidders, including retail investors?
questions.explanation: The government has reserved 5% of the auction amount in every auction for non-competitive buyers, including retail investors.
hints: Wrong: not the reservation given in the workbook.
Wrong: not the reservation given in the workbook.
Wrong: 20% is the limit for gold ETFs in bank gold deposit schemes.
Correct: 5% of each auction.

questions.q: For every unit issued, a Gold ETF holds physical gold of what purity (or gold receipts)?
questions.explanation: For every unit of a gold ETF issued, the fund holds physical gold of 99.5% purity or gold receipts.
hints: Wrong: 91.6% is 22-carat jewellery gold.
Wrong: the workbook specifies 99.5%.
Correct: 99.5% purity.
Wrong: the workbook specifies 99.5%.

questions.q: What is the key weakness of the deterministic method of calculating the retirement corpus?
options: It does not adjust expenses for inflation
It assumes constant returns and inflation and ignores sequence-of-returns risk
It is too complex to explain to clients
It always overstates the corpus required
questions.explanation: The deterministic method holds return and inflation constant and cannot see sequence-of-returns risk, so a plan that looks adequate on paper may fail.
hints: Wrong: it does inflate expenses to retirement and uses a real rate.
Correct: it ignores volatility and the order of returns.
Wrong: the workbook says it is easy to compute and explain.
Wrong: the case study shows it can understate, not overstate, the need.

questions.q: The widely cited '4 per cent' safe withdrawal rule was derived by:
options: William Bengen in 1994, using US data
The NPS Trust for annuity pricing
questions.explanation: The 4% rule was derived by William Bengen in 1994 using long-run United States data. Indian research suggests about 3-3.5% for a 30-year horizon.
hints: Wrong: PFRDA did not derive the 4% rule.
Correct: Bengen, 1994, US data.
Wrong: Markowitz is known for portfolio theory, not the 4% rule.
Wrong: the NPS Trust has no role in deriving withdrawal rules.

questions.q: Kiran wants a corpus of ₹1 crore in 25 years. If his investments earn 12% a year (monthly compounding, investments at month-end), approximately how much must he invest every month?
questions.explanation: PMT(12%/12, 300, 0, −1,00,00,000, 0) ≈ ₹5,322, the figure the workbook also uses for ₹1 crore in 25 years at 12%.
hints: Wrong: ₹1 crore ÷ 300 months ignores returns entirely.
Correct: PMT gives about ₹5,322.
Wrong: this does not match the PMT calculation.
Wrong: ₹10,515 is the requirement over 25 years at 8%.

questions.q: Once a person has retired, the workbook suggests that growth assets should form:
options: Not more than 25% to 30% of the portfolio
Zero; the portfolio should be entirely in deposits
questions.explanation: In retirement the portfolio should be predominantly income-oriented, with not more than 25% to 30% in growth assets to beat inflation.
hints: Wrong: 50-60% is the middle earning years guideline.
Wrong: this is far too aggressive for retirees.
Correct: up to 25-30% growth assets.
Wrong: some growth exposure is advised to beat inflation.

questions.q: On normal exit (superannuation), a Government sector NPS subscriber with a corpus above ₹12 lakh must use at least what share for an annuity?
questions.explanation: A Government sector subscriber may withdraw up to 60% as lump sum on superannuation; at least 40% must be used to buy an annuity.
hints: Wrong: 20% is the minimum for Non-Government subscribers.
Wrong: 60% is the maximum lump sum, not the annuity share.
Correct: at least 40% annuitisation.
Wrong: 80% annuitisation applies on premature exit.

questions.q: An All Citizen subscriber with a corpus of ₹15 lakh exits NPS prematurely. What is the rule?
options: The entire corpus can be withdrawn
Up to 20% as lump sum; at least 80% must buy an annuity
Up to 60% as lump sum; at least 40% annuity
Up to 80% as lump sum; at least 20% annuity
questions.explanation: On premature exit, up to 20% may be withdrawn as lump sum and at least 80% must be used to purchase an annuity. Full withdrawal is allowed only if the corpus is up to ₹5 lakh.
hints: Wrong: full withdrawal on premature exit is allowed only up to ₹5 lakh.
Correct: 20:80 on premature exit.
Wrong: 60:40 is Government normal exit.
Wrong: 80:20 is Non-Government normal exit.

questions.q: For a 30-year-old subscriber in Auto choice Life Cycle 75 (High), what is the equity allocation?
questions.explanation: Up to age 35, LC75 allocates 75% to equity (75/10/15 across E/C/G), tapering thereafter to 15% at 55.
hints: Wrong: 35% is LC Aggressive's terminal equity at 55 and above.
Wrong: 25% is LC25's equity up to 35.
Correct: 75% equity up to age 35.
Wrong: 50% is LC50's (and LC Aggressive's) equity up to 35.

questions.q: Who is the settlor of the NPS Trust?
options: Axis Bank, as the Trustee Bank
questions.explanation: The NPS Trust is set up under the Indian Trusts Act and PFRDA is the settlor of the NPS Trust.
hints: Wrong: the Trustee Bank only handles funds.
Wrong: the CRA is a record-keeping intermediary.
Wrong: the Ministry of Finance is not the settlor.
Correct: PFRDA is the settlor.

questions.q: Which entity is currently the custodian appointed by PFRDA for NPS securities?
questions.explanation: The custodian currently appointed by PFRDA is Deutsche Bank, engaged for a five-year term from 1 April 2022; it holds securities in the name of the NPS Trust.
hints: Correct: Deutsche Bank is the custodian.
Wrong: Axis Bank is the Trustee Bank.
Wrong: NSDL is not the NPS custodian in the workbook.
Wrong: SBI is a sponsor of a pension fund, not the custodian.

questions.q: An investor made quarterly SIP investments on different dates and wants the rate of return on the whole series of cash flows. Which Excel function is most suitable?
questions.explanation: The XIRR function calculates the internal rate of return for an investment with multiple cash flows on different dates.
hints: Correct: XIRR handles irregular dated cash flows.
Wrong: PMT calculates a periodic payment.
Wrong: PV calculates present value.
Wrong: NPER calculates the number of periods.

questions.q: Which benchmark does the workbook consider better suited to a gilt fund?
questions.explanation: While Crisil STBEX suits a short-term bond fund, a gilt fund is better benchmarked against the ICICI Securities' Sovereign Bond Indices.
hints: Wrong: STBEX suits short-term bond funds.
Correct: a sovereign bond index for a gilt fund.
Wrong: Nifty 50 is an equity benchmark.
Wrong: Sensex is an equity benchmark.

questions.q: What is the maximum investment in the Post Office Monthly Income Scheme for a single-holder account?
questions.explanation: POMIS: minimum ₹1,500; maximum ₹9 lakh for a single account and ₹15 lakh for a joint account.
hints: Correct: ₹9 lakh single.
Wrong: ₹15 lakh is the joint limit.
Wrong: ₹30 lakh is the SCSS limit.
Wrong: this is half the single-holder limit given in the workbook.

questions.q: What portion of the employer's EPF contribution is diverted to the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS)?
questions.explanation: 8.33% (subject to limits) of the employer's contribution is diverted to the EPS; the Central Government also contributes 1.16%.
hints: Correct: 8.33% goes to EPS.
Wrong: 1.16% is the Central Government's contribution to EPS.
Wrong: 3.67% is the balance of the employer's 12% that stays in EPF.
Wrong: 12% is the full employer contribution.

questions.q: A 'step-up' in periodic savings means:
options: Switching from equity to debt as retirement nears
Investing a lump sum when markets fall
Raising the SIP each year in line with income increases
questions.explanation: The workbook suggests stepping up periodic savings each year to keep pace with income, for example raising savings by 10% after a 10% salary hike.
hints: Wrong: after retirement the focus is distribution, not stepping up SIPs.
Wrong: that is de-risking or rebalancing.
Wrong: that is market timing, not step-up.
Correct: increase savings with income.

questions.q: In a diversified retirement income plan, annuity income is best earmarked for:
questions.explanation: Earmark guaranteed payouts like pension and annuity for mandatory and essential expenses, and limit annuity use to these since it is a low-yield product.
hints: Correct: guaranteed income should cover essentials.
Wrong: discretionary goals can be funded from other sources.
Wrong: mutual funds bring growth; annuities do not.
Wrong: bonds are suggested for medium-term goals such as travel.

questions.q: Which retirement income source has the primary advantage that the income tends to rise with inflation?
options: Post Office Monthly Income Scheme interest
questions.explanation: The primary advantage of rental income is that it is protected from inflation, i.e. the income goes up with inflation.
hints: Wrong: POMIS interest is fixed for the deposit term.
Wrong: SCSS interest is fixed for the deposit term.
Wrong: a level annuity pays the same amount and loses real value.
Correct: rents rise with inflation.

questions.q: An encumbrance certificate issued by the sub-registrar's office is used to:
options: Transfer ownership from seller to buyer
Approve the building plan of an apartment
Show all recorded transactions on a property, confirming the holder's title is clear
Apply for electricity and water connections
questions.explanation: An encumbrance certificate lists all transactions on the property, including sales, purchases and mortgages, and is used as confirmation that the holder has title.
hints: Wrong: the sale deed transfers ownership.
Wrong: plan approval relates to the Katha or local authority approvals.
Correct: it records transactions and confirms clear title.
Wrong: the Katha certificate is used for utility connections.

questions.q: When must a Power of Attorney be mandatorily registered?
options: Only when the donee is a family member
Only when it is a general PoA
When it creates an interest in immovable property
questions.explanation: A PoA needs to be mandatorily registered only if it creates interest in an immovable property.
hints: Wrong: the relationship of the donee does not matter.
Wrong: not every PoA needs registration.
Wrong: the type (general or specific) is not the test.
Correct: registration is compulsory for immovable property interests.

questions.q: What minimum net worth must an entity have to register as a Point of Presence for NPS?
options: ₹2 crore, including paid-up equity capital of ₹50 lakh
questions.explanation: A PoP must have a minimum net worth of ₹2 crore, including minimum paid-up equity capital of ₹50 lakh (not applicable for APY-only entities and Government departments).
hints: Correct: ₹2 crore including ₹50 lakh paid-up.
Wrong: this is far below the PoP requirement.
Wrong: ₹50 crore is the Pension Fund requirement.
Wrong: ₹100 crore is the CRA requirement.

questions.q: If a grievance escalated to the NPS Trust is not resolved within how many days may the subscriber approach the Ombudsman?
questions.explanation: If the complaint forwarded to the NPS Trust remains unresolved after 21 days, the subscriber can appeal to the Ombudsman.
hints: Correct: 21 days at the NPS Trust.
Wrong: 45 days is the time limit to file the Ombudsman appeal.
Wrong: 90 days is the Ombudsman's time to pass an award.
Wrong: 30 days is the resolution time at the intermediary.
